newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC MOVE TO ENGLAND SEEN AS "NON-STARTER".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC MOVE TO ENGLAND SEEN AS "NON-STARTER".

text.p: Scottish giants Glasgow Celtic said on Wednesday they had considered a move to the English premier league but the league responded by saying the idea was a non-starter.

"It is something that has been discussed," Celtic managing director Fergus McCann acknowledged when asked about a newspaper report linking Celtic to the lucrative English game. "However, it has not been taken any further."

And a premier league spokesman said: "There is no proposal on the table. They are merely newspaper reports from what we understand and from those reports this would appear to be a non-starter from whatever route you travel."
The report, published in the Glasgow Evening Times, said Celtic had considered a take-over of a premier league club as a way into English soccer.
It said London side Wimbledon, who have limited finances and a tiny support base, would be the obvious target for a buyout.
Celtic, alongside city rivals Rangers, dominate Scottish football.
Between them the two sides have won 81 league championships. Scotland's other sides have combined to conquer the country's premier division just 19 times.
A move to England would provide Celtic with stiffer opposition, a higher international profile and more money from sponsorship and television deals.
But it would also rob Scotland's other sides of one of their most lucrative and glamorous fixtures.
